subject.title: Feature: Streaming TTS pipeline for voice calls (sentence-level LLM→TTS→audio)

question: Should the classic voice pipeline gain provider-generic partial-response and streaming-speech APIs, and which provider/carrier pair should define the initial supported semantics?
rationale: The issue crosses the embedded-agent output contract, public plugin speech API, carrier playback behavior, and fallback and billing policy; repository evidence cannot safely choose those permanent product boundaries.

options.title: Design generic contracts first
options.body: Add optional partial-spoken-text and streaming-audio plugin capabilities, then prove them with one provider/carrier pair and compatibility fallback.

options.title: Run a narrow experiment
options.body: Keep the new path private to the voice-call plugin and initially support only ElevenLabs with Twilio before deciding whether to publish a general API.

options.title: Prefer realtime providers
options.body: Leave the classic pipeline buffered and direct latency-sensitive deployments to the existing full-duplex realtime architecture.

recommendation.title: Design generic contracts first
recommendation.body: Add optional partial-spoken-text and streaming-audio plugin capabilities, then prove them with one provider/carrier pair and compatibility fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history across the voice-call plugin, carrier providers, TTS integration, and realtime/classic architecture boundary.
